content: March 2025: tj-actions/changed-files (~23,000 repos) had its version tags rewritten by attackers to a malicious commit, exfiltrating CI secrets from every workflow that ran during the compromised window. Root cause: tag pins (e.g. @v7) are mutable references anyone with repo write access (or an account compromise) can repoint. GitHub added org-level SHA-pinning enforcement policy in Aug 2025. Best practice: pin every third-party action to a full 40-char commit SHA, not a tag or branch.
